title: WPMS/1206/2012 of SWAMI DAYANAND SARASWATI SUKHANAND CAREER Vs ADDITIONAL SECRETARY AVAS AND ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 1206 of 2012
Swami Dayanand Saraswati Sukhanand
Career Public School Educational Society ...Petitioner
Versus
Additional Secretary Avas, Uttarakhand
and others ÖRespondents
Present : Mr. Siddharth Singh, Counsel for the petitioner.
 Mr. R. C. Arya, Standing Counsel for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent no.1.
 Mr. Pankaj Purohit, Counsel for respondent nos. 2 and 3.
 Mr. Siddharth Sah, Counsel for respondent no.4.

Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. Heard Mr. Siddharth Singh, Counsel for the
petitioner, Mr. R. C. Arya, Standing Counsel for the State
of Uttarakhand/respondent no.1, Mr. Pankaj Purohit,
Counsel for respondent nos. 2 and 3 and Mr. Siddharth
Sah, Counsel for respondent no.4.

2. The petitioner before this Court has admittedly
raised the construction in violation of the buildings law.
He has constructed structure where he is running higher
secondary school which is situated in Chandreshwar
Nagar, Rishikesh is an area of Haridwar Development
Authority (hereinafter referred to as ìHDAî) and hence
governed by the Uttar Pradesh Urban Planning and
Development Act, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as ìActî).
3. This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner
challenging certain orders dated 5.6.2012, 31.3.2010 and
15.5.2008. While construction was going on ceiling
orders were passed by respondent no.3 under Section
28(A)(1) of the Act on 15.5.2008. Section 28(A)(1) of the
Act reads as under:-
ì28-A. Power to seal unauthorised
development.- (1) It shall be lawful for the
Vice-Chairman or an officer empowered by him

2
in this behalf, as the case may be, at any time
before or after making an order for the removal
or discontinuance of any development under
Section 27 or Section 28 to make any order
directing the sealing of such development in a
development area in such manner as may be
prescribed for the purposes of carrying out the
provisions of this Act.î
4. The order dated 15.5.2008 was challenged by the
petitioner in appeal before the Divisional Commissioner
which was dismissed on 31.3.2010. Aggrieved the
petitioner moved a revision before respondent no.1 under
Section 41 of the Act which was also dismissed on
5.6.2012. Aggrieved the petitioner has filed the writ
petition before this Court. By an interim order dated
21.6.2012, the learned Single Judge of this Court had
directed that the HDA to consider the compounding
application of the petitioner and meanwhile the disputed
premises may not be sealed. On the strength of the said
interim order, the disputed construction has not been
sealed and the order of the appellate authority as well as
State Government have not been implemented.
5. It is admitted by the petitioner that the disputed
construction has been raised by him without any
sanction map from the HDA. The only contention of the
petitioner is that since he has already raised the
construction he is now wiling to pay the compounding
charges. This contention of the petitioner cannot be
accepted by this Court. There are certain categories of
construction which are compoundable and other which
are not compoundable. This Court is presently not in a
position to evaluate as to whether the construction is
compoundable or not. However, the contention of the
petitioner is that it is an entirely new building and

3
compounding application of the petitioner has already
been rejected by the HDA and so is the appeal now he is
before the State Government in the revision under
Section 41 of the Act.
6. On these set of facts no interference, as prayed by
the petitioner can be called for where the petitioner
admits that he has raised the construction without
taking prior sanction from the HAD, and where the
construction is admittedly an unauthorized construction.
The writ petition is without merit and is hereby
dismissed.
7. No order as to costs.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 8.10.2012
Kuldeep
